title: microburst amplification via scale-down pacing and admission jitter
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Summary:
Several customers reported sudden latency spikes and 5xx errors during short traffic microbursts over the last 48 hours. The root cause is an emergent interaction between the scale-down pacing heuristic and per-tenant admission jitter which amplified transient queue growth into actual reserved-pool shortfalls. This ticket drives the production bugfix, mitigation, and post-incident follow-ups for dedicated capacity autoscaling behavior.

Observed behavior:
- Short (5–20s) increases in per-tenant request rate produced long-tail queueing at the tenant admission layer.
- The scale-down pacing algorithm interpreted the short lull after the burst as a sustained drop and initiated an aggressive downscale (slot decommit) within the autoscaler's cool-down window.
- Admission jitter (randomized token allocation backoffs) caused reordering and a concentrated retry wave, which re-created peak demand before new allocations had warmed up, causing reserved pools to run below required headroom.
- Result: transient increase in request failures (429/503) and high tail latency for affected tenants; several customers opened escalations.

Why this is unique/different from previous incidents:
Many past tickets focused on warmup-credit leaks, headroom misestimation, or lease-table races. This incident is about an amplification loop between a scale-down pacing decision and admission-side jitter/retry behavior. The autoscaler did not violate its own safety limits, but the combined system dynamics produced a customer-visible capacity shortfall during microbursts.
reproduction_steps: Simulate 10s microburst for a VIP tenant against a coldish reserved pool (30% initial headroom)
Inject admission jitter (random 10-200ms backoff) on allocation attempts
Observe scale controller decision to decommit slots within 30s of the microburst trough
Trigger second burst within 10-20s after downscale and watch queue latency and 5xx rate
impact_summary: Impacted ~6 mid-size tenants on dedicated clusters over the incident window; peak error rates up to 8% for affected tenants, spikes lasted 15–90s per incident before fallback to hosted models triggered; several escalations to support and two enterprise accounts flagged as high priority.
mitigation_applied: Hotfix #1 (rollout 2026-03-02 02:10 UTC): temporarily extend scale-down cool-down from 30s to 180s for all dedicated clusters in region eu-west-1
Hotfix #2 (rollout 2026-03-02 03:00 UTC): add admission smoothing layer to cap instantaneous retry bursts (max 50 concurrent retry tokens per tenant)
Customer comms: posted incident update to Status page + Slack and emailed affected account contacts
root_cause: No single component exceeded thresholds. Root cause is system-level feedback loop: (1) aggressive scale-down pacing reduced headroom too quickly after a microburst, (2) admission-side randomized backoffs compressed retries into a second amplified wave, and (3) cold allocations require nonzero warmup that could not replenish capacity fast enough, leading to transient reserved-pool underprovisioning.

2026-03-02 02:10 UTC: Hotfix #1 deployed to eu-west-1; immediate reduction in errors observed

postmortem_actions: 1) Update autoscaler: implement burst-detection override to prevent any downscale within 180s of an observed >2x short-window spike (owner: Mateo)
2) Modify admission layer: replace randomized per-request jitter with token-bucket smoothing + backpressure signaling (owner: Priya Nair)
3) Telemetry: add composite metric 'microburst-amplification-index' combining per-tenant burst slope, downscale events, and retry concentration (owner: Observability team)
4) Runbook: add explicit customer communication template for short microburst capacity impacts (owner: SRE/Support)
5) Regression tests: add chaos test injecting admission jitter and verifying no reserved-pool underprovisioning (owner: Infra QA)
6) Account review: proactively reach out to affected enterprise customers and offer capacity credits/consult
